Performers
Emma Eames (soprano) Documented

The Discography of American Historical Recordings describes the matrix as “Soprano vocal solo, with piano” and names no pianist; the Romophone booklet lists this track among those with piano and gives no accompanist.

[4] [3] [1]
Work version
Beach’s Browning setting, complete: both settings of the opening lines, then the rest of the poem. It is the second of two songs on one 12-inch Victor side, after George Henschel’s “Spring”. The key is D♭ major. Inferred, not documented

The pairing with Henschel’s “Spring” is documented by the Discography of American Historical Recordings and the July 1909 catalogue, and the Romophone track list gives “Spring” and “The Year’s at the Spring” as parts of one matrix. That the track is the whole song is inferred by comparing its sung pitches with the vocal part of the 1900 edition (B♭ version, read in D♭): the leaps to E♭, F and G♭ of the first setting fall in the first eleven seconds, and the restart on p. 4 follows at about fifteen seconds. No source states it. The key is inferred from the closing chord and from the key printed on the label of Eames’s 1905 recording of the song. The edition she sang from (the 1900 print offers B♭ and D♭ versions) has not been seen.

[4] [6] [3] [7]
Recorded
1908-05-18 Documented

Matrix C-6203, take 1. The Archive file name and the Romophone track list give the same date.

[4] [3] [1]
Place
New York, New York, United States Documented

Recording place from the Discography of American Historical Recordings; no studio address is given.

[4]
Label
Victor Talking Machine Company, Red Seal (12-inch single-faced) Documented

The July 1909 catalogue lists the disc on the Emma Eames page at $3.00.

[5] [6]
Catalogue
Victor 88008 Documented

The same number had carried Eames’s 1905 recording of the song with Hahn’s “L’Incrédule” (listed in the May 1908 catalogue); the July 1909 catalogue lists the 1908 pairing under it. The Discography of American Historical Recordings also lists IRCC-194 and AGSB-22 reissues of this matrix.

[4] [5] [6] [3]
Matrix, take, sides
C-6203, take 1 Documented

Both songs are on one matrix, which the Discography of American Historical Recordings titles “Spring” with “Year’s at the spring” as an additional title, and which it notes was “Also recorded as C-2314”, the 1905 recording. The Romophone booklet gives C 6203-1.

[4] [3]
Transfer
Ward Marston, transfers and audio restoration; Ward Marston, producer; Virginia Barder, executive producer. Romophone 81001-2, CD 2, track 13. Documented

These credits are printed for the whole set. The Internet Archive item (whose own text gives the set number as 81000-2) names the set and the track but no separate engineer for the file; the person who ripped and uploaded it is not credited as an engineer.

[3] [1]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The Archive descriptions date the set to 1993; a Beach discography gives 1995, and the booklet scan prints no year. The dates of the disc transfer and the restoration are not stated. The Internet Archive upload of 8 April 2025 is a copying event, not a transfer date.

[3] [2] [11]
Processing
Restoration by Ward Marston for the Romophone CD, with no settings stated; the Internet Archive derives its VBR MP3 from an uploaded WAV or FLAC rip of the CD. Documented

The closing chord of this track is D♭ major at concert pitch, within about a tenth of a semitone of A = 440 Hz. Two other Internet Archive transfers of the same disc (item 78_springbyearofthespring_146_06, the second labelled IRCC 194-A) play about three per cent faster, half a semitone sharp of this file. Stylus, equalisation and noise reduction are not documented. About five seconds of silence follow the last chord.

[3] [1] [2]
Composition rights
Out of copyright: Beach died in 1944 and Browning in 1889. Inferred, not documented

Life-plus-70 terms have run out for both; the first edition was published in the United States in 1900. This covers the song, not modern editions.

[7]
Recording rights
US public domain: first published by July 1909 on Victor 88008 (recorded 18 May 1908). The Archive item carries the Public Domain Mark. Documented

Selected under the project’s us-published-before-cutoff rule: a recording first published before 1923 had exhausted its federal term by 31 December 2021. The July 1909 catalogue is the dated source for 1909 as the latest year of first publication. The audio is the Romophone restoration by Ward Marston. The Public Domain Mark was applied by the uploader, is a statement by the person who identified the work, and is not the basis for publication. The scanned booklet carries no copyright notice for the transfers (its only © line is for the essay; the tray insert is not in the scan), and the track is one continuous performance in score order. The Ninth Circuit held in ABS Entertainment v. CBS (2018) that a remaster distinguished only by change of medium, declicking or noise reduction generally lacks the originality needed for a new copyright. No source consulted shows Romophone or Marston dedicating the restoration to the public domain, and a claim outside the United States has not been ruled out; the booklet’s text and the set’s compilation are not claimed as public domain.

Amy Beach, The Year’s at the Spring, Op. 44 No. 1. Emma Eames, soprano, with piano. Victor 88008, matrix C-6203 take 1, New York, 18 May 1908. Transfer and restoration by Ward Marston, Romophone 81001-2, via the Internet Archive. Recording: US public domain (published by 1909). Rights statement
